name: Pablo Roy
life: “I still remember mending sails while my family went out to celebrate.” People around Studio Boulevard know Pablo by a small Wednesday habit. Pablo waits by the window where the whole crossing can be seen without leaning into the road.
voice: I did every winter repair while my spouse sailed. I think dry-land hours ought to count.
appearance: Pablo is easy to recognize by a blunt cut just below the ears and a heart-shaped face and prominent ears. Usually dressed in a long navy raincoat with a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light, Pablo listens with the head tilted a little to the left when listening.
personality: Pablo thinks best while walking. Sitting beneath someone's office clock makes Pablo sound more certain than they feel, an effect close friends have learned to distrust.
agenda: To count winter repair time fairly.
family: Jody Hewitt is Pablo’s second cousin. Pablo checks the date twice. Jody brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *A closing hour*, Jody says, “I was going to post a complaint. I wrote my week's opening hours on his birthday card because I need a day off too.”
connections: Gareth Parker (former spouse). Former spouses decide whether a Sunday afloat and an hour repairing ashore have equal weight.

reactions.situation: A spouse asks to count repair hours toward Sunday time
reactions.response: Pablo checks the maintenance log before treating Sundays as the only contribution.

reactions.situation: An argument on the pavement makes a bystander feel unsafe
reactions.response: Pablo puts distance between the frightened person and the argument and asks nearby staff for help.

reactions.response: Pablo asks them to walk to the corner together and listen until the corner comes.
